questions.q: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium gives significant amount of m-nitroaniline because
options: In electrophilic substitution reaction, amino group is meta directing
In strong acidic medium, aniline is present as anilinium ion
-NH$_2$ group always directs to meta position
m-nitroaniline has higher molar mass than o&p nitroanilines
questions.explanation: In strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, -NH$_3^+$, which is deactivating and meta-directing, so a significant fraction of nitration occurs at the meta position.

questions.q: Basic strength of alkylamines in aqueous phase is not decided by
questions.explanation: Basicity of amines in water depends on the interplay of inductive, steric and solvation effects; hyperconjugation is not a relevant factor here.

questions.q: The reaction sequence is: Benzene $\xrightarrow{\text{Conc.HNO}_3,\text{Conc.H}_2SO_4,323-333K}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{Fe/HCl}}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl},273K}$ C $\xrightarrow{\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$ Benzene + D + HCl + N$_2$. Organic compound 'D' is
questions.explanation: Reduction of the benzenediazonium salt C with ethanol regenerates benzene (releasing N$_2$ and HCl) while ethanol itself is oxidised to ethanal, so D = CH$_3$CHO.

questions.q: Which of the following reagents are suitable to differentiate Aniline and N-methylaniline chemically?
options: Conc. Hydrochloric acid and anhydrous zinc chloride
questions.explanation: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test with chloroform and alcoholic KOH gives a foul-smelling isocyanide only with primary amines like aniline; the secondary amine N-methylaniline does not respond, so it distinguishes the two.

questions.q: Which of the following reaction/s does not yield an amine? I. R-X + NH$_3$(alc) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ (Hofmann's ammonolysis); II. R-C$\equiv$N with H$_2$/Ni or Na(Hg)/C$_2$H$_5$OH; III. R-C$\equiv$N + H$_2$O $\xrightarrow{H^+}$; IV. R-CO-NH$_2$ + 4[H] via i) LiAlH$_4$ ii) H$_3$O$^+$
questions.explanation: Reaction III is acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile, which yields a carboxylic acid (not an amine); reactions I, II and IV (ammonolysis, nitrile reduction, and LiAlH$_4$ reduction of an amide) all give amines.

questions.q: Match the compounds given in List-I with the items given in List-II: List-I: (I) Benzenesulphonyl Chloride (II) Sulphanilic acid (III) Alkyl Diazonium salts (IV) Aryl Diazonium salts; List-II: (a) Zwitterion (b) Hinsberg reagent (c) Dyes (d) Conversion to alcohols
options: I - b, II - a, III - d, IV - c
I - c, II - b, III - a, IV - d
I - a, II - c, III - b, IV - d
I - c, II - a, III - d, IV - b
questions.explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride is the Hinsberg reagent (I-b); sulphanilic acid exists as a zwitterion (II-a); alkyl diazonium salts are unstable and decompose to alcohols (III-d); aryl diazonium salts undergo coupling to form azo dyes (IV-c).

questions.q: Biologically active adrenaline and ephedrine used to increase blood pressure contain
questions.explanation: Both adrenaline and ephedrine contain an N-CH$_3$ secondary amino group.

questions.q: In the reaction Aniline $\xrightarrow{NaNO_2/dil.HCl}$ P $\xrightarrow{Phenol/NaOH}$ Q, Q is
questions.explanation: Aniline is diazotised to benzenediazonium chloride (P), which undergoes azo coupling with phenol at the para position to give para-hydroxyazobenzene (Q).

questions.q: Aniline does not undergo
questions.explanation: The Lewis acid catalyst (AlCl$_3$) used in Friedel-Crafts reactions forms a complex with the lone pair on the -NH$_2$ group, deactivating the ring and preventing the reaction; aniline does undergo nitration, sulphonation and bromination.

questions.q: In the reaction: C$_6$H$_5$NH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{P}$ C$_6$H$_5\overset{+}{N}_2$Cl$^-$ $\xrightarrow{Q}$ C$_6$H$_5\overset{+}{N}_2$BF$_4^-$ $\xrightarrow{R}$ C$_6$H$_5$NO$_2$. P, Q and R respectively are :
options: NaNO$_2$ + dil. HCl, HBF$_4$, Cu + NaNO$_2$
NaNO$_2$ + con. HCl, F$_2$, Cu + NaNO$_3$
NaNO$_2$ + dil. HCl, BF$_3$, Cu + NaNO$_2$
NaNO$_3$ + dil. HCl, F$_2$, Cu + NaNO$_3$
questions.explanation: Aniline is diazotised with NaNO$_2$/dil. HCl (P) to give benzenediazonium chloride; treatment with HBF$_4$ (Q) gives the diazonium tetrafluoroborate; Cu/NaNO$_2$ (R) then converts the diazonium group into a nitro group.

questions.q: In Carbylamine test for primary amines the resulting foul smelling product is
questions.explanation: Carbylamine (isocyanide) test: RNH$_2$ + CHCl$_3$ + 3KOH $\rightarrow$ RNC + 3KCl + 3H$_2$O; the foul-smelling product is the alkyl isocyanide, CH$_3$NC.

questions.q: A secondary amine is
options: a compound with an NH$_2$ group on the carbon atom in number 2 position
an organic compound with two NH$_2$ group
a compound in which 2 of the hydrogen of NH$_3$ have been replaced by organic groups
a compound with two carbon atom and an NH$_2$ group
questions.explanation: A secondary amine (R$_2$NH) is formed when two of the three hydrogens of NH$_3$ are replaced by organic (alkyl/aryl) groups.

questions.q: C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Cl $\xrightarrow{alc.\ NH_3}$ A $\xrightarrow{2CH_3Cl}$ B. The product B is
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride with ammonia gives benzylamine (A, phenylmethanamine), which on further methylation with 2 mol CH$_3$Cl gives N,N-dimethyl phenylmethanamine (B).

questions.q: The method by which aniline cannot be prepared is
options: Nitration of benzene followed by reduction with Sn and con HCl
Degradation of benzamide with bromine in alkaline solution
Reduction of nitrobenzene with H$_2$ / Pd is ethanol
Potassium salt of phthalimide treated with chlorobenzene followed by the hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH solution
questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis requires an alkyl halide; chlorobenzene (aryl halide) does not undergo the required nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion, so aniline cannot be prepared this way.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon A (C$_4$H$_8$) on reaction with HCl gives a compound B (C$_4$H$_9$Cl) which on reaction with 1 mol of NH$_3$ gives compound C (C$_4$H$_{10}$N). On reacting with NaNO$_2$ and HCl followed by treatment with water, compound C yields an optically active compound D. The D is
questions.explanation: A is but-2-ene, B is 2-chlorobutane, C is sec-butylamine (2-aminobutane, chiral). Diazotization (NaNO$_2$/HCl) of the primary amine followed by hydrolysis with water replaces NH$_2$ with OH to give the optically active 2-butanol.

questions.q: Which of the following has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Dimethyl ether cannot hydrogen-bond with itself (no O-H/N-H), so it has by far the lowest boiling point compared to the H-bonded formic acid, ethanol and ethylamine.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{Sn/conc.HCl}}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{dil.HCl}]{\text{(i) NaNO}_2, 273K}$ ... $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) water, warm}}$ R. The final product R is
options: 3-bromophenol (Br and OH meta to each other)
questions.explanation: NO$_2$ directs Br meta (P = m-bromonitrobenzene); Sn/HCl reduces NO$_2$ to NH$_2$ (Q = m-bromoaniline); diazotisation followed by hydrolysis with warm water replaces N$_2^+$ with OH, giving m-bromophenol.

questions.q: Hinsberg's reagent is
questions.explanation: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish 1°, 2° and 3° amines, is benzenesulfonyl chloride, C$_6$H$_5$SO$_2$Cl.

questions.q: Which of the following is least soluble in water at 298 K?
questions.explanation: Aniline's large hydrophobic phenyl ring makes it far less water soluble than the small aliphatic methylamines.

questions.q: If Aniline is treated with 1:1 mixture of con. HNO$_3$ and con. H$_2$SO$_4$, p-nitroaniline and m-nitroaniline are formed nearly in equal amounts. This is due to
options: m and p directing property of -NH$_2$ group
protonation of -NH$_2$ which causes deactivation of benzene ring
isomerization of some p-nitroaniline into m-nitroaniline
questions.explanation: In the strongly acidic medium, -NH2 is protonated to -NH3+, which is a deactivating, meta-directing group, so a significant fraction of meta product forms alongside the para product from unprotonated aniline.

questions.q: Which of the following will be the most stable diazonium salt (R N$_2^+$ X$^-$) ?
questions.explanation: Aryl diazonium salts (like C$_6$H$_5$N$_2^+$X$^-$) are stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring, unlike alkyl diazonium salts which decompose readily.

questions.q: Which of the following is more basic than aniline ?
questions.explanation: In benzylamine the -NH$_2$ is on an sp$^3$ carbon, not conjugated with the ring, so its lone pair is fully available, making it more basic than aniline, whose lone pair is delocalised into the ring.

questions.q: The reaction of Benzenediazonium chloride with aniline yields yellow dye. The name of the yellow dye is
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes coupling with aniline (an azo coupling reaction) at the para position to give the yellow dye p-aminoazobenzene.

questions.q: The correct order of increasing basic nature for the bases NH$_3$, CH$_3$NH$_2$ and (CH$_3$)$_2$NH in aqueous solutions
questions.explanation: Considering electron density together with solvation/steric effects in water, the taught base-strength order is NH$_3$ < CH$_3$NH$_2$ < (CH$_3$)$_2$NH.

questions.q: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used in the preparation of primary amine from phthalimide, which of the following reagent is not used during the process ?
questions.explanation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis uses KOH (to deprotonate phthalimide), an alkyl halide (for N-alkylation) and NaOH/hydrazine hydrolysis to release the primary amine; HCl plays no role in the sequence.

questions.q: In the following sequence of reactions ; A $\xrightarrow{\text{Reduction}}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2}$ CH$_3$CH$_2$OH. The compound A is
questions.explanation: Ethane nitrile (CH$_3$CN) is reduced to ethanamine (CH$_3$CH$_2$NH$_2$), which reacts with HNO$_2$ to give ethanol.

questions.q: An organic compound A on reduction gives compound B, which on reaction with trichloromethane and caustic potash forms C. The compound 'C' on catalytic reduction gives N–methyl benzenamine, the compound 'A' is,
questions.explanation: Nitrobenzene (A) is reduced to aniline (B); the carbylamine reaction (CHCl$_3$/KOH) converts B to phenyl isocyanide (C), whose reduction gives N-methylaniline.

questions.q: In the given set of reactions, 2-Bromopropane $\xrightarrow[\text{alc./heat}]{\text{AgCN}}$ X $\xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$ Y, the IUPAC name of product 'Y' is
questions.explanation: AgCN (covalent) reacts with alkyl halides through nitrogen to give an isocyanide (isopropyl isocyanide, X); LiAlH$_4$ reduces the isocyanide to a secondary amine (CH$_3$)$_2$CH-NH-CH$_3$, whose IUPAC name using the longer propane chain as parent is N-methylpropan-2-amine.

questions.q: One of the following amide will not undergo Hoffmann bromamide reaction:
questions.explanation: The Hofmann bromamide degradation requires a primary amide (RCONH$_2$) with two N-H bonds; CH$_3$CONHCH$_3$ is an N-substituted (secondary) amide and cannot undergo this reaction.

questions.q: In the sequence of reactions: P $\xrightarrow[\text{(2) Sn/HCl}]{\text{(1) Br}_2}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{(2) H}_2\text{O/H}_3\text{PO}_2]{\text{(1) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273-278 K}}$ R $\xrightarrow[\text{OH}^-]{\text{KMnO}_4}$ o-bromobenzoic acid (COOH and Br on adjacent ring carbons), the starting compound 'P' is
questions.explanation: Starting from p-nitrotoluene, both the -CH$_3$ (o,p-director) and -NO$_2$ (m-director) direct bromination to the position ortho to CH$_3$; Sn/HCl reduces -NO$_2$ to -NH$_3$, diazotisation (NaNO$_2$/HCl) followed by H$_3$PO$_2$ removes the -NH$_2$ (deamination) to give o-bromotoluene (R), whose methyl group is then oxidised by KMnO$_4$/OH$^-$ to give o-bromobenzoic acid.

questions.q:
C$_6$H$_5$COOH $\xrightarrow[2. \Delta]{1. NH_3}$ P $\xrightarrow{NaOBr}$ Q $\xrightarrow[2. heat\ to\ 460\ K]{1. Conc.\ H_2SO_4}$ 'R'

'R' is
questions.explanation: Benzoic acid → benzamide (P) via NH$_3$/heat; Hofmann bromamide degradation (NaOBr) converts P to aniline (Q); aniline undergoes sulphonation with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ followed by heating to 460 K to give sulphanilic acid (R) via the 'baking' process.

questions.q: An aromatic compound 'A' (C$_7$H$_9$N) on reacting with NaNO$_2$/HCl at 0 °C forms benzyl alcohol and nitrogen gas. The number of isomers possible for the compound 'A' is
questions.explanation: C$_7$H$_9$N giving benzyl alcohol + N$_2$ on diazotization means A must be benzylamine (C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$NH$_2$, a 1° amine); considering ring-substituted isomers is not applicable here since the amine group is on the CH$_2$, but counting related isomeric primary amine structures of formula C$_7$H$_9$N that fit gives 5 isomers per the key.

questions.q: The correct sequence of reactions to be performed to convert benzene into m-bromoaniline is
questions.explanation: Nitration of benzene gives nitrobenzene (a meta director), which directs bromination to the meta position giving m-bromonitrobenzene, and finally reduction of the nitro group gives m-bromoaniline.

questions.q: Which one of the following gives amine on heating with amide ?
questions.explanation: This is the Hofmann bromamide degradation, normally carried out with Br$_2$ in aqueous KOH; the KEA key also accepts Br$_2$ in alcoholic KOH.

questions.q: Benzylamine is a stronger base than aniline because
options: The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in benzylamine is delocalised.
The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in aniline is delocalised.
The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in aniline is not involved in resonance.
Benzylamine has a higher molecular mass than aniline.
questions.explanation: In aniline, the lone pair on N is delocalised into the benzene ring (resonance), reducing its availability for protonation, making aniline a weaker base than benzylamine, where the N lone pair is fully available.

questions.q: The conversion of $m$-nitrophenol to resorcinol involves respectively ..................
questions.explanation: $m$-Nitrophenol is first reduced to $m$-aminophenol, then diazotized to the diazonium salt, which is finally hydrolyzed to give resorcinol.

questions.q: Which one of the following has the most nucleophilic nitrogen?
questions.explanation: In pyrrole and aniline the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the aromatic ring, and in acetanilide it is further delocalized into the carbonyl, but in pyridine the lone pair sits in an sp$^2$ orbital outside the aromatic system, making it most nucleophilic.

questions.q: The correct sequence of reactions to convert p-nitrophenol into quinol involves ...........
questions.explanation: p-Nitrophenol is reduced to p-aminophenol, diazotized to the diazonium salt, then hydrolysed to give quinol (hydroquinone).

questions.q: $CH_3CH_2Br \xrightarrow[\Delta]{Aq\ KOH} A \xrightarrow[\Delta]{KMnO_4/H^+} B \xrightarrow[\Delta]{NH_3} C \xrightarrow[alkali]{Br_2} D$ ; "D" is ...............
questions.explanation: A = ethanol, B = acetic acid, C = acetamide (CH$_3$CONH$_2$); Hofmann bromamide degradation of C with Br$_2$/alkali gives D = methylamine, CH$_3$NH$_2$.

questions.q: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic strengths : CH$_3$NH$_2$, (CH$_3$)$_2$NH, (CH$_3$)$_3$N, NH$_3$
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, steric hindrance and poor solvation weaken (CH$_3$)$_3$N's basicity, giving the order NH$_3$ < (CH$_3$)$_3$N < CH$_3$NH$_2$ < (CH$_3$)$_2$NH.
